messages:
amy_support: customer reports most console graph panels hang on 'Loading...' since about 09:12 UTC. They hit 'Try again' and the graph never appears. they pasted the browser console and got a 502 from /analytics/query.

amy_support: repro steps i followed: 1) open console -> dashboards -> select customer org id X123 -> open the Errors dashboard -> pick last 7d -> some panels show data, others stuck.

amy_support: curl we saw:
```
GET /api/v1/analytics/query?queryId=9a8f...  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Correlation-ID: cor-2112345678

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Server: edge
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "upstream read timeout", "backend": "analytics-worker-7" }
```

ben_oncall: thanks amy. correlation id noted. any recent deploys around 09:00-09:10?

sara_product: customer says this started after they refreshed dashboards at 09:11 — could be a heavy retained query or time range change. which panels are failing?

amy_support: failing panels are ones that fan out many subqueries (per-tenant metrics, long range = 90d). smaller single-series panels return fine. i tried reducing to 30d and most panels load.

chris_analytics: sounds like query fanout + queue saturation. check analytics.query_queue_length and clickhouse pending queries. also check prefix/KV cache hits for these ranges.

ben_oncall: im pulling logs from analytics-worker-7 now. will grep for cor-2112345678 and related trace.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: analytics-worker v2.14.3 -> v2.14.4 by chris_analytics at 2025-11-02T08:58:12Z :shipit:

ben_oncall: log excerpt:
```
2025-11-02T09:12:03Z ERROR handler.go:142 request cor-2112345678 upstream read timeout after 30s 
stack: queryfanout.exec -> clickhouse.Exec -> context deadline exceeded
```

chris_analytics: that 30s timeout matches our proxy read timeout. v2.14.4 changed parallel subquery windowing, might increase fanout for certain aggregation queries. rolling back is an option but let's triage first.

amy_support: customer also mentions UI shows an exclamation tooltip: "Query timed out (analytics)." they provided a sample query id 9a8f-- if we need to replay.

ben_oncall: action items: 1) chris confirm whether v2.14.4 has the new windowing default and if it can be toggled per-route; 2) sara add a temporary status note for affected dashboards; 3) amy collect one failing full query payload for replay; 4) set alert on analytics.query_queue_length > 100 for 5m.

chris_analytics: confirmed — the default windowing was widened in 2.14.4. can revert to previous logic via feature flag analytics.windowing=legacy per-deployment. i'll test toggling on analytics-worker-7.

ben_oncall: toggled feature flag on worker-7, retrying the customer's query now.

amy_support: retry from support account -> panels loaded within 4s after toggle. customer confirmed on call that graphs repopulated.

amy_support: repro notes for runbook: when console graphs return 5xx/upstream timeouts: 1) check correlation-id in browser devtools, 2) grep analytics-worker logs, 3) verify recent analytics deploys, 4) consider toggling analytics.windowing to legacy, 5) for immediate relief, reduce dashboard time range or enable sample-rate-throttle, 6) follow-up: create perf test for large-fanout queries.

sara_product: i'll open a ticket to track roll-forward vs revert and make sure this gets prioritized for a patch that preserves previous windowing for high-fanout queries. assigning to chris.

chris_analytics: i'll do a patch release with the toggle defaulted to legacy for next 24h and add a regression test.

ben_oncall: closing the urgent incident — monitoring alert created and runbook updated. amy please send the customer a short summary and next steps. :thumbsup:

amy_support: will do, sending message now and logging case# SUP-2025-489. thanks all.
